title: Entropy Scaled First Principle Derivation of Gravitational Acceleration from Sequential Oscillatory-Electromagnetic Reverberation Within a Confined Boundary at Threshold Frequency
content: This paper introduces a theoretical framework for the emergence of gravitational acceleration from recursive photonic interactions governed by threshold frequency and entropy-scaled delay. We propose that mass, space, and time arise not as fundamental primitives but as emergent structures from photonic recursion confined within a boundary condition. Through phase-locked constructive interference at specific temporal intervals, quantized units of spacetime—referred to as voxels—are formed. Each voxel stores energy through recursive light folding, regulated by a mechanism we term skip emission logic, wherein sub-threshold emissions are withheld until recursive alignment permits voxel formation. The resulting delay structure gives rise to radial acceleration, interpreted macroscopically as gravity.The model derives gravitational acceleration from first principles by scaling voxel energy via system-wide entropy density, without invoking geometric curvature or exotic fields. Furthermore, the observer’s limited dimensional bandwidth is incorporated through a square-root compression principle, ensuring a consistent mapping between internal recursion and observable force. The theory introduces several new constructs—including recursive delay, skip emission logic, and observer dimensional reduction—that together form a closed explanatory loop for mass-energy emergence and gravitational behavior. This framework offers testable predictions and a novel path toward unifying quantum optics, thermodynamics, and spacetime geometry within a single photonic encoding architecture.
